title: The Gloria (Luke 2:14)
hook: the angels' song from Bethlehem, silent in Advent and Lent
carry: glory to god in the highest

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kyrie eleison: Lord, have mercy, kept in Greek inside the Latin Mass. Your line was mercy, three times.

Go back eighty days, to the shepherds. A night on the hills outside Bethlehem: sheep, cold, a fire, nothing happening. Then an angel, a light, terror, and the news: a child is born. And suddenly, Luke says, there's a whole crowd of angels, a heavenly army, praising God. It's the first Christmas song, and it's one line long. Every Sunday, right after asking for mercy, the church picks up that song and keeps going. For four weeks before Christmas and six weeks before Easter, it goes quiet. And when it comes back, the bells ring.
screen: `THE SHEPHERDS' HILLSIDE.` → `A CROWD OF ANGELS.` → `THE FIRST CHRISTMAS SONG.`

segments.voice: Here's the angels' line, in the Douay-Rheims: "Glory to God in the highest; and on earth peace to men of good will." In Latin, Gloria in excelsis Deo. That's where the hymn starts, but the Gloria at Mass goes much further. Christians in the first few centuries kept singing after that line, adding praise upon praise. In Latin: laudamus te, benedicimus te, adoramus te, glorificamus te. Praise, blessing, adoring, glorifying. Then it turns to Jesus as the Lamb of God, who takes away the world's sins, and asks his mercy. It ends with the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, like the Glory Be you learned, but bigger. That's why it's sometimes called the greater doxology: the Glory Be is the little glory-word, and this is the big one. Notice where it sits. Right after the church asks for mercy, it bursts into praise. Sorry, then glory. And it isn't sung every week. In Advent, the weeks before Christmas, it's left out, so the angels' song can come back new on Christmas night. In Lent, it's silent too. On Holy Thursday, it's sung while every bell in the church rings, and then the bells go silent until Easter. At the Easter Vigil, the Gloria returns, and the bells ring again. One small scholar's note: the King James Bible reads good will toward men. The Latin tradition reads peace to men of good will. The difference is one letter in some Greek manuscripts.
screen: `THE ANGELS' SONG.` · `PRAISE UPON PRAISE.` · `SORRY, THEN GLORY.` · `SILENT, THEN BELLS.` · then, large: `GLORY TO GOD IN THE HIGHEST.`

segments.voice: If you pray, say or hum one line: glory to God in the highest. Quietly is fine, tunelessly is fine; the shepherds weren't choir material either. If you don't pray, find one thing that's simply good, something that asks for nothing back, say so out loud, that's beautiful, and sit with it.
Gloria. The angels' song from Bethlehem, grown into a hymn of praise at Mass, and kept silent in Advent and Lent. Today's word.
Your line: glory to God in the highest. The angels' one-line song, still being sung. See you tomorrow.

chat.says: Why do Catholics leave out the Gloria some weeks?
options: It's left out in Advent and Lent, so it comes back new at Christmas and Easter.
It's only sung when a bishop visits, to make that Mass more festive.
It's long, so parishes save it for weeks when the readings are short.
chat.meaning: The Gloria goes quiet in Advent and Lent, so the angels' song returns new on Christmas night and at the Easter Vigil.

Gloria in excelsis Deo.meaning: Latin: glory to God in the highest

Advent.meaning: the four weeks before Christmas, when the Gloria is left out

Lent.meaning: the weeks before Easter, when the Gloria is silent

Easter Vigil.meaning: the night service before Easter, when the Gloria returns

notes: Douay-Rheims Luke 2:14 given from memory; confirm.
The later lines of the Gloria are paraphrased from the traditional text, not quoted from ICEL.
GIRM 53: sung on Sundays outside Advent and Lent, on solemnities and feasts. Bells at the Gloria of Holy Thursday and the Easter Vigil: confirm.

Textual note: Greek manuscripts differ between eudokia (nominative, 'good will toward men', KJV) and eudokias (genitive, 'men of good will', Vulgate/Douay). 'One letter' refers to the final sigma. Confirm.
'Go back eighty days': the shepherds were day 26 on this path; 107 − 26 = 81. Confirm or adjust.
The Gloria is also sung at Christmas Midnight Mass after Advent's silence.
